metadata.scope: Measured CPU results in this environment; no GPU results or inferred timings.

timing.question: How does measured execution scale when the mathematical transform is held fixed?
timing.protocol: Complex128 inputs; one CPU thread; independent direct summation, compiled radix-2, and SciPy FFT. Eleven randomized-order batches per method and size. JIT compilation, input generation, and explicit root/permutation planning are excluded. Every call allocates its output; SciPy internal dispatch and workspace handling remain included. Direct DFT stops at N=2048.
timing.limitations: Bands are empirical 10th–90th percentiles of per-call batch averages, not confidence intervals. One machine and one implementation of each algorithm do not establish universal speedups. Cached, repeated inputs are used. The direct method is a compiled scalar sum, not optimized dense BLAS.

accuracy.question: Does a small normwise FFT error guarantee accurate weak spectral coefficients?
accuracy.protocol: Three deterministic phase/seed replicates per N, signal family, precision and method. Each binary input is cast BEFORE its independent direct DFT at 80 decimal digits. Error is relative Euclidean norm. Complex64 and complex128 output types are checked. Weak-bin error refers to bin 7 of the represented input, not the unrounded analytic signal.
accuracy.limitations: These are finite empirical samples, not worst-case stability bounds. Binary32 input quantization is measured separately. In the dynamic-range case, quantization may already obscure the intended weak mode before the FFT starts. Near-zero coefficient relative errors are intrinsically sensitive; normwise conditioning is still one.

padding.question: Can padding to a slightly longer FFT make the SAME linear convolution faster?
padding.protocol: Two fixed real arrays of length 8191; each method computes two forward complex FFTs, a pointwise product and one inverse FFT, then truncates to the required 16381 outputs. Eleven randomized batches at each of 16 neighboring valid transform lengths. Every result is checked against a separate direct convolution.
padding.limitations: Performance reflects SciPy on this CPU. Longer is not always faster, prime length is not automatically slow on every implementation, and no speedup changes the O(N log N) algorithmic class. Padding is valid here because all lengths exceed the full linear-convolution support.

poisson.question: Can an almost-zero discrete residual coexist with a visibly inaccurate PDE solution?
poisson.protocol: Periodic [0,2π)² grid, u=exp(0.8 cos x+0.6 sin y) up to a constant, and the analytically differentiated source f=−Δu. This analytic field has infinitely many Fourier modes. Both source and reference are centered on each grid; removed source means are reported. Solve with either the continuous spectral symbol k²+l² or the five-point finite-difference symbol. Report the residual of the selected discrete operator separately from error against the sampled exact field.
poisson.limitations: Smooth periodic manufactured data favor spectral convergence. The experiment does not cover nonsmooth fields or nonperiodic boundaries. Observed orders below the 1e−12 error threshold are omitted because roundoff dominates. Projecting the sampled source is necessary for discrete compatibility and is explicitly recorded.
